tools.name: draw_diagram
tools.description: Workflow. Checks, describes, and draws a diagram. With errors it returns each one with line, column, and a fix hint and draws nothing: fix the source and call again. When valid it returns the quality warnings (take the icon and group-type suggestions), an outline to check the meaning, the size, and the SVG for light, dark, or both (theme= on the header picks the colour theme). You cannot see an SVG, so over MCP the answer carries none unless you pass svg "always" (picturesOmitted says so); svg "never" checks most cheaply. Give viewUrl to the person: the drawing lives in the link and nothing is saved on Plotwork; pngUrl and svgUrl download it; saveCommand, when given, saves it in a repository. Every check runs on the drawing either way. Set embedSource true to save an SVG in a repository or publish one to edit later, so read_diagram gives the source back (anyone with the file can read it). detail "full" adds the whole outline. To change an existing diagram use edit_diagram, or read_diagram for a picture. Saves no file; never throws on bad source. Replaces the validate_diagram, outline_diagram and render_diagram calls.

source.description: Diagram source. The first line is the header: flow "Title", sequence "Title", schema "Title", git "Title", gantt "Title", class "Title", state "Title", timeline "Title", journey "Title", mindmap "Title", treemap "Title", pie "Title", quadrant "Title", layers "Title", c4 "Title", matrix "Title", sankey "Title", xychart "Title", tree "Title", swimlane "Title", requirement "Title", block "Title", packet "Title", kanban "Title", radar "Title", usecase "Title", venn "Title", fishbone "Title", or wardley "Title".

schemes.description: light, dark, or both (the default): the light picture and the dark one a dark page needs.

theme.description: Colour theme for this drawing, over the header's theme=.

detail.description: summary (the default), or full: the whole outline, and the source embedded in each SVG.

svg.description: auto (the default): over MCP the SVG text stays out of the answer (picturesOmitted). always returns it. never draws nothing, cheapest. Checks run either way. The HTTP API treats auto as always.

embedSource.description: Write the source into each SVG so read_diagram can give it back. Set it when you save the SVG in a repository or publish it to edit later; anyone with the file or link can then read the source.

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

inputSchema.description: Diagram source and what to return: the color schemes to draw and how much detail.

tools.name: edit_diagram
tools.description: Workflow. Changes diagram source with typed operations, on every kind, and checks the result. Each op and its fields: rename (target, to: an id everywhere it is used, or a label), set (target, or from and to for an edge, or target "header"; option, value, null removes it), add_node (id, label, type, options; into a block or after a statement; statement for a whole line), remove (target, with its block and edges), add_edge (from, to, label, arrow, options), remove_edge (from, to, label), move (target, into: a block, or null for the top level), replace_text (find, replace, all). Untouched lines keep their comments and layout. Each op reports applied, or why not with a hint, and a failed one is skipped. svg "never" (the default) lays nothing out; auto or always draws as draw_diagram does, with viewUrl and saveCommand. Replaces rewriting the source by hand and the draw_diagram check.

source.description: Diagram source; the first line is the header, such as flow "Title" (draw_diagram lists every kind).

to.description: rename: the new name. Edges: the end.

type.description: add_node: node type, or statement word (c4 person, tree dir).

statement.description: add_node: the whole line, for a kind with no plain node statement.

into.description: A block; null is the top level.

svg.description: never (the default) draws nothing; auto or always draws like draw_diagram.

schemes.description: light, dark, or both (the default): the light picture and the dark one a dark page needs.

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

inputSchema.description: Diagram source and the edits to make to it.

tools.name: convert_mermaid
tools.description: Workflow. Converts one Mermaid diagram (flowchart or graph, sequenceDiagram, erDiagram, gitGraph, gantt, classDiagram, stateDiagram, timeline, journey, mindmap, treemap-beta or treemap, pie, quadrantChart, C4Context or C4Container or C4Component or C4Dynamic or C4Deployment, sankey-beta or sankey, xychart-beta or xychart, treeView-beta or treeView, requirementDiagram, block-beta or block, packet or packet-beta, kanban, radar-beta or radar, usecase-beta or usecase, venn-beta or venn, ishikawa-beta or ishikawa, wardley-beta, architecture-beta, zenuml) to Plotwork source. Returns the source, a diagnostic with a hint for everything dropped or changed (styling, links, activations), the check of the result with its icon and group-type suggestions, and an outline; render true also draws it, with picturesOmitted, viewUrl, pngUrl, and saveCommand as in draw_diagram. A Mermaid type Plotwork does not draw comes back as one diagnostic saying what to do instead. Deterministic: never throws on bad input, does not fetch URLs or read files. For a whole Markdown document use sync_markdown with convertMermaid true. Replaces the convert, validate_diagram, outline_diagram and render_diagram calls.

source.description: One Mermaid diagram: a flowchart or graph, sequenceDiagram, erDiagram, gitGraph, gantt, classDiagram, stateDiagram, timeline, journey, mindmap, treemap-beta or treemap, pie, quadrantChart, C4Context or C4Container or C4Component or C4Dynamic or C4Deployment, sankey-beta or sankey, xychart-beta or xychart, treeView-beta or treeView, requirementDiagram, block-beta or block, packet or packet-beta, kanban, radar-beta or radar, usecase-beta or usecase, venn-beta or venn, ishikawa-beta or ishikawa, wardley-beta, architecture-beta, or zenuml. Front matter and %%{init}%% directives are allowed and are dropped. Send the text inside a mermaid fence, without the fence.

lenient.description: false (the default): a line that cannot be read stops the conversion, so nothing is converted with a line missing. true: such a line is skipped with a warning and the rest is converted.

render.description: Also draw the converted diagram, in the color schemes schemes names.

schemes.description: light, dark, or both (the default): the light picture and the dark one a dark page needs.

detail.description: summary (the default), or full: the whole outline, and the source embedded in each SVG.

svg.description: auto (the default): over MCP the SVG text stays out of the answer (picturesOmitted). always returns it. never draws nothing, cheapest. Checks run either way. The HTTP API treats auto as always.

embedSource.description: Write the source into each SVG so read_diagram can give it back. Set it when you save the SVG in a repository or publish it to edit later; anyone with the file or link can then read the source.

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

tools.name: import_source
tools.description: Workflow. Turns a file into a finished diagram in one call: a database schema, an API spec, infrastructure as code, manifests, a software catalog, a CI workflow, CSV or JSON data, a folder listing, or a git log. get_diagram_syntax with topic import-formats says what each format reads, draws, and takes. Prefer it to drawing by hand whenever the person has such a file: send its text, never a path, or every file of a folder in files. Returns the source, diagnostics pointing into the file for anything left out, coverage, parts (every diagram of a split file), the validation, an outline, viewUrl, and saveCommand. It runs no code and reads no file or URL. Replaces validate_diagram and outline_diagram.

format.description: What the text is; get_diagram_syntax with topic import-formats describes each.

text.description: The file content, as text. Send text or files, not both.

files.description: The files of a folder, for a format that spans files; the others read the first.

path.description: The file path, such as infra/network.tf; diagnostics name it.

title.description: The diagram title; taken from the file when left out.

partsPage.description: Which page of parts to return when a split import has more than 24 diagrams: 1 (default) is the first 24.

view.description: The picture of a format drawn several ways.

chart.description: csv, json: the chart; auto picks.

tables.description: Tables to draw, by name or prefix*.

groupBy.description: How things are framed; module is the default.

root.description: The root, stack, template, or draw.io page of several to draw.

icons.description: off: no icons, as settings with icons off.

inputSchema.description: A file of another format to turn into Plotwork source.

tools.name: map_icons
tools.description: Workflow. Finds an icon for each of up to 40 service or product names in one call, such as the services of an architecture. For every name it returns the best provider:name icon with a confidence (exact, strong, or ambiguous) and up to 3 alternatives. It never guesses: a name that could mean several icons (a kind of service several clouds offer, or a match by idea only) comes back with resolved false and candidates to choose from, and a name that matches nothing is listed in gaps with a neutral fallback icon. Set provider to the cloud the architecture runs on, so "queue" finds that cloud's product first. Reads the bundled icons and, when hosted, the organisation icons (org:name). Replaces up to 40 search_icons calls.

names.description: Services, products, or ideas to find icons for, written as the user wrote them ("S3", "Postgres", "load balancer"). Up to 40 names of up to 80 characters.

provider.description: The cloud the architecture runs on. A name is looked up there first, so "queue" finds aws:sqs for aws. Omit it when the names are not tied to one provider.

inputSchema.description: Names to find icons for, and an optional provider to look in first.

tools.name: sync_markdown
tools.description: Workflow. Turns the diagram fences of a Markdown document into pictures, as data. Send the whole document and its path. Returns the rewritten document (each fence folded into a "Diagram source" section with the picture and a text description, the rest byte for byte unchanged), the SVG files to write (paths from the repository root), and a report per fence with errors at lines of your document. convertMermaid true first turns each convertible mermaid fence into a diagram fence; one that cannot convert or has errors is left as it was and reported. Then write markdown to documentPath and each file to its path, and review the diff. mode "check" only reports. The SVGs can be large: files "none" returns each file's path, bytes, sha256, and viewUrl instead, and page with pageSize returns the files a page at a time. Writes no file itself. Limits: 10000000 characters, 30 diagrams, 2000000 bytes of output; caps says when one stopped work. Replaces the convert, validate, render and sync steps for every fence in a document.

markdown.description: The whole Markdown document, exactly as it is on disk, with its line endings. Up to 10000000 characters.

documentPath.description: Where the document lives, relative to the repository root, with forward slashes, for example docs/guide.md. Picture links and file paths are worked out from it.

assetsDir.description: The directory for the SVG files, relative to the repository root. The default is assets/diagrams next to the document.

prefix.description: Text put in front of every picture file name, for documents that share one assets directory. By default a titled diagram is named from its title and an untitled one from the document name.

convertMermaid.description: When true, every ```mermaid fence that can be converted is replaced by a ```diagram fence first, then drawn. Fences that cannot be converted are left exactly as they were and reported.

mode.description: sync (the default) returns the rewritten document and the files to write. check changes nothing: it only reports whether a picture is stale or a fence would convert.

files.description: inline (the default) returns each SVG file with its content. none returns each with path, bytes, sha256, and viewUrl instead, so the answer stays small.

page.description: Which page of files to return, from 1; pictures are paged in document order, a light and a dark file together.

pageSize.description: Pictures per page, at most 30. Setting page or pageSize turns paging on.

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

inputSchema.description: A Markdown document and how to turn its diagram fences into pictures.

tools.name: suggest_diagram
tools.description: Workflow. Picks the kind of diagram for a request in plain words, such as "permission matrix for these endpoints and roles" or "where our cloud spend goes", with optional pasted data (a table, a list, numbers by period). Returns up to 3 kinds, best first, each with a one-sentence reason, a confidence, the statements to use, and a short starter source that parses, built from the names and numbers in the request and data. Call it when you are unsure which kind fits, then edit the starter and call draw_diagram. Replaces reading every kind in get_diagram_syntax to choose one.

request.description: What the picture is for, in plain words, such as "permission matrix for these endpoints and roles" or "how a refund moves between support and billing".

data.description: Optional text to draw from: a pasted table, a list, numbers by period, or notes. Names and numbers in it are used in the starters.

inputSchema.description: A request in plain words and optional data to draw from.

tools.name: plan_document_diagrams
tools.description: Workflow. Reads a whole document (Markdown, HTML, or plain text pasted from Confluence, Notion, or Google Docs), splits it by its headings, and returns the sections a picture would help: the heading and its line, the kind, a one-sentence reason, a confidence, and a starter source drafted from the section's own lists, tables, numbers, and dates. Sections that read well as text, or already have a diagram, are left out. Draws nothing and changes nothing. Replaces reading the document section by section and choosing a kind for each.

document.description: The whole document: Markdown, plain text pasted from Confluence, Notion, or Google Docs, or HTML. Up to 10000000 characters.

maxSuggestions.description: Most sections to suggest a picture for, up to 12. The strongest are kept, in document order. The default is 8.

inputSchema.description: A document to read for the sections a picture would help.

tools.name: find_pattern
tools.description: Workflow. Finds a ready-made, checked architecture diagram for a request such as "three tier network", "serverless api", or "two availability zones". Send the request in plain words, and optionally a provider (neutral, aws, azure, or gcp), tags, a diagram kind, and a limit of up to 5. Returns the best matches first, each with an id, a one-sentence summary, tags, and the flavours it comes in, never the source. Start here when the user asks for a common architecture: a pattern is already validated, laid out, and described, so you adapt it instead of drawing from nothing. Replaces searching the documentation for an example to copy.

query.description: The architecture wanted, in plain words, such as "three tier network".

provider.description: Only patterns that come in this flavour: neutral, aws, azure, or gcp.

tags.description: Tags every result must have, such as "load balancer". Up to 5.

kind.description: Only patterns of this diagram kind: flow, sequence, schema, git, gantt, class, state, timeline, journey, mindmap, treemap, pie, quadrant, layers, c4, matrix, sankey, xychart, tree, swimlane, requirement, block, packet, kanban, radar, usecase, venn, fishbone, or wardley.

limit.description: Most results to return, up to 5.

inputSchema.description: Words that describe the architecture wanted, and optional filters.

tools.name: get_pattern
tools.description: Workflow. Returns one pattern filled for a flavour: its valid Plotwork source, every slot with its meaning and value, the advice on what to keep, rename, and split, and the structure as groups, overlays, and nodes. Send the id from find_pattern, a provider (neutral by default, or aws, azure, gcp), and optionally slot values such as {"office": "Branch office"} to name its parts. Edit the source for anything a slot does not cover, then validate it. file true also returns it as a pattern file to change and publish. An unknown id, flavour, or slot, or a value with a quote in it, comes back as a problem with a fix, not as an error. Replaces searching for an example and copying it by hand.

id.description: The pattern id, as find_pattern returns it, such as three-tier-network.

provider.description: neutral (generic glyphs, no vendor names; the default), or aws, azure, or gcp for that provider's icons. Not every pattern comes in every flavour; the answer lists the ones it has.

slots.description: Slot values keyed by slot id, such as {"office": "Branch office"}: plain text of up to 60 characters, no quotes or line breaks. Omit a slot to keep its default. get_pattern lists the slots and what they mean.

file.description: true also returns the whole pattern as a pattern file, to edit, check_pattern and publish_pattern.

inputSchema.description: A pattern id, the flavour to draw, and the slot values to use.

tools.name: draw_from_pattern
tools.description: Workflow. Fills a pattern and draws it in one call. Send the id from find_pattern, a provider (neutral by default, or aws, azure, gcp), optional slot values that rename its parts, and the schemes. Returns the source, the slots, the advice on adapting it, the quality warnings, a plain-text outline, and the SVG for light, dark, or both. Use it when a pattern fits with only names changed; use get_pattern to edit the source first. An unknown id, flavour, or slot comes back as a problem with a fix. svg, picturesOmitted, viewUrl, pngUrl, saveCommand, and detail work as in draw_diagram. Replaces the get_pattern, validate_diagram, outline_diagram and render_diagram calls.

id.description: The pattern id, as find_pattern returns it, such as three-tier-network.

provider.description: neutral (generic glyphs, no vendor names; the default), or aws, azure, or gcp for that provider's icons. Not every pattern comes in every flavour; the answer lists the ones it has.

slots.description: Slot values keyed by slot id, such as {"office": "Branch office"}: plain text of up to 60 characters, no quotes or line breaks. Omit a slot to keep its default. get_pattern lists the slots and what they mean.

schemes.description: light, dark, or both (the default): the light picture and the dark one a dark page needs.

detail.description: summary (the default), or full: the whole outline, and the source embedded in each SVG.

svg.description: auto (the default): over MCP the SVG text stays out of the answer (picturesOmitted). always returns it. never draws nothing, cheapest. Checks run either way. The HTTP API treats auto as always.

embedSource.description: Write the source into each SVG so read_diagram can give it back. Set it when you save the SVG in a repository or publish it to edit later; anyone with the file or link can then read the source.

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

inputSchema.description: A pattern id, the flavour and slot values to use, and what to return.

tools.name: read_diagram
tools.description: Read the source of an existing Plotwork SVG so you can edit the diagram. Send the text of an .svg file as svg, or a hosted link (https://cdn.plotwork.dev/d/<22 characters>.svg) as url. Returns the exact source, its kind, the stored diagram id if it was published, and a parse check. Call it first when asked to change a diagram that already exists, then edit the source and call draw_diagram (or edit_diagram); next says how to save or publish it again. Only a picture saved with embedSource true (or by sync_markdown) carries its source; otherwise status is no-source, with the title, outline, and labels to rebuild it from. A text that is not an SVG and a refused or unreachable link come back as data. Only cdn.plotwork.dev and cdn-preview.plotwork.dev are fetched (https, no redirects, 5 seconds, 1 MB); svg reads nothing from the network.

svg.description: The text of a Plotwork SVG: the content of an .svg file in the repository. Send this or url, not both.

url.description: The link of a hosted Plotwork picture, https://cdn.plotwork.dev/d/<22 characters>.svg. Only Plotwork's own picture hosts are fetched. Send this or svg, not both.

inputSchema.description: The text of a Plotwork SVG, or the link of a hosted one.

tools.name: compare_diagrams
tools.description: Compare two versions of a diagram by meaning, for a pull request review. Send before and after, each as source, the text of a Plotwork SVG that carries its source, or a cdn.plotwork.dev link. Returns every statement added, removed, renamed (by id or label), moved to another block, or changed (options, type, edge arrow or label), with counts and a plain-language summary; markdown true adds a block ready to paste as a comment. Reordered or reformatted lines are no change. A side with no source is reported, not an error. Lays nothing out; fetches only a link.

before.description: The old diagram: source, the text of a Plotwork SVG that carries its source, or a cdn.plotwork.dev link.

after.description: The new diagram, in any of the same three forms.

markdown.description: Also return a Markdown block ready to paste as a pull request comment.

inputSchema.description: Two versions of a diagram to compare.

tools.name: check_pattern
tools.description: Check a pattern file before you publish it to an organisation or save it to import. A pattern is a diagram an organisation approves: fixed parts every team draws the same, and {{slot}} markers in quoted labels for what each team fills in. Start from get_pattern with file true. Returns every problem with its field and a fix, or each flavour filled with its defaults, to send to draw_diagram. Saves nothing.

pattern.description: The pattern file. Every field is described at https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.pattern.json; get_pattern with file true gives one to start from.

inputSchema.description: A pattern file to check before it is published or imported.

tools.name: get_diagram_syntax
tools.description: Read the diagram language as data. Call it once with no kind before your first diagram: the overview, the tables every kind shares (node types, arrows including dotted ..> for asynchronous calls, animated and numbered lines, icon sets, size limits, how to edit an existing SVG), and one line about each kind. For one kind in full, call it again with kind set to it: its statements, limits, and a tested example. kind flow adds the group types (type=), overlays, stack= marks, and a complete cloud architecture example; build the group tree top-down with type=, one node per service, and icons from map_icons or search_icons. For a common architecture, find_pattern gives a checked diagram to adapt. topic import-formats lists what import_source reads.

kind.description: The one kind to read in full. Omit it for the overview: the language every kind shares and one line about each kind.

topic.description: import-formats: what import_source reads, draws, and takes, a line each.

tools.name: validate_diagram
tools.description: Check diagram source without drawing it: every error in one pass, each with line, column, and a fix hint, plus quality warnings. An icon a label names for certain is drawn already; W204 gives the exact icon=provider:name for a node whose label names a product it does not draw (a brand whose name is also an everyday word, or every match under icons=off), W205 the type= for a group whose name matches a group type, and W206 flags an overlay framing a node that is not its member. These suggestions are not applied for you: add one, or icon=none to keep a node plain, and validate again. Prefer draw_diagram, which checks, describes, and draws in one call.

source.description: Diagram source; the first line is the header, such as flow "Title" (draw_diagram lists every kind).

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

tools.name: render_diagram
tools.description: Render valid source to a self-contained, accessible SVG in the light, dark, or auto scheme and an optional colour theme, with its pixel size and quality warnings. Source with errors fails with its diagnostics. Set embedSource true to save the SVG in a repository, so read_diagram can give the source back. Prefer draw_diagram, which validates, outlines, and renders in one call.

source.description: Diagram source; the first line is the header, such as flow "Title" (draw_diagram lists every kind).

scheme.description: Color scheme to paint with: light, dark, or auto for one picture that follows the reader's light or dark setting.

theme.description: Colour theme for this drawing, over the header's theme=.

idPrefix.description: Prefix for element ids; set it when inlining several diagrams into one page.

embedSource.description: Write the source into the SVG metadata so read_diagram can give it back. Set it true when you save the SVG into a repository; anyone with the file can then read the source. Default false.

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

tools.name: outline_diagram
tools.description: Describe valid diagram source as plain text: participants, steps, tables, and connections in reading order, to check the diagram says what you meant or to use as alt text. Source with errors fails with diagnostics. Does not render. Prefer draw_diagram, which returns the outline with the check and the pictures.

source.description: Diagram source; the first line is the header, such as flow "Title" (draw_diagram lists every kind).

settings.description: The repo's plotwork.config.json, if any. Schema: https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.config.json

tools.name: search_icons
tools.description: Find bundled icon names by keyword, idea, product, or abbreviation ("postgres", "token exchange", "s3", "cosmos db"). Returns set:name references, best first, at most 100, such as lucide:database, simple:postgresql, aws:lambda. Cloud products are in one set per provider (aws, gcp, azure, alibaba, oci, ibm, cloudflare, digitalocean, vercel), with every official aws, azure, and gcp icon; <provider>:cloud is the provider, for a group. Use it before setting icon= or a name in stack=. Search with the product name exactly as the user wrote it and take the first result; never invent a name, because an unknown icon is an error. For several names prefer map_icons: up to 40 in one call, and it never guesses. Hosted calls also find the organisation icons, as org:name.

q.description: Words to look for: a name such as "database", an idea such as "token exchange", or a cloud product such as "lambda" or "gke".

inputSchema.description: Query parameters for an icon search.

instructions: Draws flow, sequence, database schema, git graph, Gantt chart, class diagram, state, timeline, user journey, mind map, treemap, share chart, quadrant chart, layered architecture, C4 diagram, matrix, Sankey diagram, XY chart, tree, swimlane, requirement diagram, block diagram, packet diagram, kanban board, radar chart, use case diagram, Venn diagram, fishbone diagram, and Wardley map diagrams from a small line-oriented text language. Prefer the workflow tools: each does the work of several single tools in one call. When you are unsure which kind of diagram fits, call suggest_diagram with the request in plain words and any data: it ranks the kinds and gives a starter that parses; for a whole document, plan_document_diagrams returns the sections a picture would help, each with a starter. When the diagram should come from a file the person has (SQL, Prisma, or Drizzle models, an OpenAPI document, a GraphQL or Protocol Buffers schema, Terraform, Bicep, ARM, Pulumi, CloudFormation, the CDK, or a serverless.yml, docker-compose, a Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, Helm, Kustomize, nginx configuration, a Backstage catalog, a Structurizr workspace, AsyncAPI documents, a GitHub Actions workflow, a GitLab CI/CD or Azure Pipelines pipeline, a dbt project, the package manifests of a JavaScript workspace, a draw.io diagram, CSV or JSON data, a folder listing, or a git log), call import_source with its text and format: it builds the whole diagram from the file in one call, and its diagnostics say what was left out get_diagram_syntax with topic import-formats says what each format reads. For a request to draw a common architecture, such as a three-tier network, a serverless API, a container platform, or a queue with workers, call find_pattern first with the request in plain words; when a pattern fits, call draw_from_pattern with its id, a provider flavour (neutral, aws, azure, or gcp), and slot values that rename its parts, or get_pattern to read and edit its source, and when nothing fits, write the diagram from scratch with draw_diagram. To make an organisation's approved pattern (a diagram with fixed parts every team draws the same and {{slot}} markers for what each team fills in), write a pattern file: get_pattern with file true gives one to start from, and https://docs.plotwork.dev/schemas/plotwork.pattern.json describes every field. Check it with check_pattern, fix every problem it names, and send each source it returns to draw_diagram; then save it as <name>.pattern.json for the Patterns tab to import. Call get_diagram_syntax once with no kind to read the shared language, and again with kind set to the kind you draw for its statements, limits, and example. Write the source and call draw_diagram: it returns every error with line, column, and hint and draws nothing until the source is valid, so fix every error and call again; once valid it returns the warnings, an outline to check the meaning, and the SVG for light and dark. You cannot look at an SVG, so the answer carries no SVG text unless you pass svg "always": it gives viewUrl for the person, saveCommand to write the files, and the pictures go to the diagram viewer. Every check ran on the drawing all the same. Pass svg "never" to check a diagram most cheaply, and svg "always" only when you need the SVG text in the answer. To change a diagram that already exists as a Plotwork SVG, a hosted link such as https://cdn.plotwork.dev/d/<22 characters>.svg or an .svg file in the repository, call read_diagram first with its url or its text, change the source it returns with edit_diagram (rename, set an option, add, remove, or move a statement) or by hand and draw_diagram, then write the SVG file again; compare_diagrams says what changed, for a review. Set embedSource true on draw_diagram whenever you save an SVG into a repository, so the file carries its source and read_diagram can give it back next time; the source is then readable by anyone who has the file. To save a valid diagram into the person's repository, run the saveCommand a drawing tool returns in a shell, changing --out to the path you want (add --theme dark for the dark picture): the Plotwork command line reads the diagram from the link on that machine, fetches nothing, and writes the SVG with its source embedded, so you never copy the SVG yourself. With no shell, draw with svg "always" and embedSource true and write the returned svg. Give viewUrl to a person to look at the diagram, and svgUrl or pngUrl to download it in their browser; neither is a file address for curl. An item with no icon= gets the icon its label names when the match is certain, such as the Postgres mark on a node labelled "Postgres", so label items with the product they are; icon=none keeps one item plain and icons=off on the header keeps them all plain. For a finished look, label flow arrows with verbs ("reads", "publishes", "deploys to") so they draw icons, add role= (data, async, identity, private) to the lines that carry those, and give groups a type=; style in get_diagram_syntax says more. Use map_icons to choose icons for many names at once; it never guesses, so choose from the candidates for an ambiguous name, and never invent an icon. To move Mermaid to Plotwork, call convert_mermaid with one diagram, read every diagnostic and its hint, then choose node types and icons; for a whole Markdown file call sync_markdown with the document, its path, and convertMermaid true, write the returned markdown and files, then review the diff. When the repository has a plotwork.config.json (or .plotwork/config.json) at its root, read it and pass it as settings to every tool that takes settings: its defaults fill the header options the source leaves out, and broken style rules come back as warnings to fix. Use validate_diagram, outline_diagram, render_diagram, and search_icons only for one fine-grained step. Choose node types and tones for meaning; colors come from the colour theme, theme=<name> on the header (plotwork, slate, ocean, forest, sunset, mono, contrast), and cannot be set one by one.
